title: What Happens in Space Without a Suit?
script: You'd survive space for 15 seconds. What if an airlock burst open and flung you into space? You wouldn't pop like a balloon. The movies got it wrong. Space is a vacuum, but that's not what kills you. The real danger is the lack of oxygen. But that's not even the strange part. The vacuum causes ebullism, where the water in your body starts to boil at your own temperature. You'd have about 15 conscious seconds before a lack of oxygen knocks you out. That's roughly the time it takes to watch a space helmet reflection for 15 seconds. You could watch the Earth spin about 2 degrees in that time. The vacuum's effect is so extreme that a NASA test subject in 1966 felt the saliva bubbling on his tongue before he blacked out. You'd want to remember that 15 seconds for next time this comes up.
